data.title: Bulls vs. Bears: Whither Credo Technology after post-earnings selloff
data.description:
Credo Technology Group (CRDO) closed more than 26% lower this week, marking its worst weekly drop in nearly two years after its Q1 results for fiscal 2027, as profitability concerns overshadowed its better-than-expected financials.

While many Seeking Alpha analysts renewed their bullish bets on the semiconductor firm after the historic selloff, a few others indicated bearish calls, giving the stock an overall rating of Buy on the SA platform.     

The Bulls

“Despite a strong Q1 earnings print, the market appears to be misreading risks and overreacting to perceived negatives,” wrote Investing Group Leader Danil Sereda in “Credo's Post-Earnings Selloff Creates Strong Buying Opportunity (Review).” “Credo Technology remains a compelling opportunity, with shares now undervalued after a 40% pullback from its peak.”

“Credo delivered 115% revenue growth, while management expects 85%+ FY2027 growth and more than $600 million optical revenue,” added SA analyst Yiannis Zourmpanos in “Credo: Why I'm Buying Again (Rating Upgrade).” “CRDO has corrected roughly 40% from $309, bringing shares near my $175-$190 buy zone around long-term technical support.”

“CRDO’s Q2 guidance implies decelerating growth, but optical business scale-up in H2 FY27 supports >85% full-year revenue growth,” wrote Uttam Dey in “Credo And The Illusion Of Its Q1 Problems (Double Upgrade).”  “The markets irrationally fear margin compression ahead, which has nothing to do with execution gaps but more to do with how prior M&A deals were structured.”

“CRDO turned in solid results, but the market is in panic mode,” noted Investing Group Leader Kumquat Research in “Credo Earnings: Waiting For A Buying Opportunity? Here It Is.”  “For those looking for a buying opportunity in CRDO stock, this is it.”

“Credo grew Q1 revenue 115% to $479 million while sustaining a 68% gross margin and 49.3% non-GAAP net margin,” argued Pythia Research in “Why I Doubled Down On Credo.”  “I believe CRDO is severely underrated not only based on its growth profile but also relative to peers in terms of connectivity and AI.”

“The selloff was a needed cool-off after an 189% run-up in Q2 and market panic about the future of copper vs. optics showing up,” added Tech Stock Pros in “The Market Made Credo Cheap, Again.” “The stock is unignorably cheap again, trailing its own historical averages and the direct peer group.”

The Bears

“CRDO's GAAP gross margins declined to 64.5% YoY, pressured by acquisition-related amortization and ongoing customer concentration risk,” opined Andres Veurink in “Credo Technology: Seems I Was Right To Be Bearish On This.” “Despite impressive YoY revenue growth, CRDO's forward P/E of 63x and flat margin guidance make the risk/reward unattractive.”

“Credo receives a Sell rating due to deteriorating margins, rising expenses, and high customer concentration despite headline revenue growth,” added Bears of Wall Street in “Credo: This Is Not A Buying Opportunity.”  “Valuation model suggests intrinsic value is ~45% below the current price, even assuming an optimistic revenue inflection in the second half.”

“The stock has just horribly broken key short-term support and also broken below the 50-week MA after earnings,” wrote Oliver Rodzianko in “Credo: Semiconductor Stocks Are Melting Down, But Some Still Deny It.” “Valuation remains elevated with a forward P/E of 33.5, and sector overvaluation risks outweigh near-term growth prospects.”

data.title: Real estate stocks post losses in August amid surging rate hike odds
data.description:
Real estate stocks closed the month of August lower, posting losses in three of the eight months.

For August, the S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) decreased 2.00% month-over-month to 280.86 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was down 2.13% to $44.11.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index declined 2.70%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index retreated 2.85%.

Comparatively, the benchmark S&P 500 index closed the month 2.62% higher.

Technology and retail earnings, a weak July jobs report, in-line inflation data, the Q2 GDP print, a rebound in cryptocurrency prices, and the doubling of the size of bond buybacks by the Treasury shaped broader market returns.

Real estate stocks were largely losing after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to bring inflation down to the central bank's 2% target at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium.

Here is a look at the XLRE price movement this month, compared to the benchmark S&P 500 index:

"The biggest takeaway for me is that Warsh isn't ready to declare victory on inflation, and he left the door open to higher rates if inflationary pressures don't improve. In terms of the forward, he gave us little in the way of guidance, but the message was clear enough, in my view," said Seeking Alpha analyst Justin Purohit.

"The one that stuck out to me was Warsh believing that the dual mandate is not in conflict with itself, which is a 'we can have our cake and eat it, too' sentiment that the bond market hates. Yields jumped when he said that line," said SA analyst Jack Bowman.

"This speech did not appease the bond market much, and I expected it not to. The market seems to think that the tough talk on inflation is just that: talk," noted Bowman.

Mortgage rates rose amid surging bond yields and ongoing Middle East conflict. However, mortgage demand did not show significant weakness, signaling strength in the housing market.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) led the weekly losers, pulling back 4.14% from the prior week to $362.36.

CoStar Group (CSGP) (-4.07% W/W to $30.91) and Public Storage (PSA) (-3.67% W/W to $302.01) followed.

This week, Public Storage's CFO for real estate, Aric Chang, stepped down from his role to pursue an opportunity at American Healthcare REIT (AHR). AHR appointed Chang CFO, effective October 1.

Digital Realty Trust (DLR) led the gainers, advancing 1.57% on a weekly basis to $188.39.

Data center stocks were largely in the green as President Donald Trump slammed communities rejecting data centers, calling the opponents 'backwards and poor'.

The data center boom is becoming a major issue in the upcoming midterm elections, with local communities pushing back on construction plans amid concerns over electricity rates and environmental impact.

Omega Healthcare Investors (OHI) was another winner, adding 0.85% to $46.38.

The week saw PACS Group agreeing to acquire 32 skilled nursing facility operations, leased from Omega Healthcare. However, financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Millrose Properties (MRP) topped the midcap gainers, advancing 4.61% to $32.02. Blackstone Mortgage Trust (BXMT) followed with a 3.42% addition to $14.20.

Apple Hospitality REIT (APLE) (-5.74% W/W to $15.60) and DiamondRock Hospitality Company (DRH) (-4.88% W/W to $12.08) were major losers in the category.

U.S. travel industry has recently suffered a setback as it tries to sustain a World Cup-driven spending boost despite weaker international visitation and new barriers for some foreign travelers. Long visa waits, high airfares, tariffs, and strict travel policies have curbed international arrivals, impacting hotel REITs.

Americold Realty Trust (COLD) (-5.26% W/W to $14.22) was also a significant decliner.

For smallcap stocks, Real REMAX Group (REAX) (-11.47% W/W to $18.67) extended losses from the previous week that saw Real Brokerage and Re/Max close their previously announced merger.

Gladstone Land (LAND) (+9.59% W/W to $9.83) topped the gainers.

data.title: Jefferies-linked fund reportedly has $500M exposure to Radiant World
data.description:
A fund managed by Jefferies (JEF) has nearly $500M worth of exposure to troubled iron ore trader Radiant World, its founder, and another entity, The Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

On Thursday, Reuters reported that Jefferies (JEF)-managed LAM Trade Finance Group II, in which the U.S. bank holds a minority stake, obtained a freezing order from London's High Court against Radiant World and several affiliated entities and individuals.

The filing named Radiant World, its founder Pinkesh Nahar, and Sapphire Minmetals, allegedly an affiliated trading firm of Radiant and Sapphire Minmetals’ chairman Rakesh Sethi, as defendants

The freezing order worth up to $499M implies that the Jefferies (JEF) fund’s exposure to Radiant and linked entities is significantly higher than previously reported and highlights its function as a key financier of the two iron ore traders.

Point Bonita, a private credit fund within Jefferies’ Leucadia Asset Management, is also facing concerns over its exposure to Radiant World. Since initially providing $35M in funding in 2021, its exposure to Radiant World jumped to hundreds of millions of dollars over four years, according to people familiar with the matter.

In April, the company signed a forbearance agreement with both Radiant and Sapphire. Those deals are typically intended to give companies that have defaulted the option to establish a payment plan and put up additional collateral instead of repaying the debt immediately.

data.title: Healthcare August recap: Moderna jumps 156% as biotech shines; DaVita sinks
data.description:
The healthcare sector (XLV) gained 4.91% in August, outperforming the broader S&P 500 (SPY), which advanced 2.68% during the month. Healthcare stocks benefited from strength in biotechnology and medical technology, while healthcare services, managed care, and selected pharmaceutical stocks remained under pressure.

Healthcare Sector Scorecard

Sector Return: +4.91% in August

Best Performer: Moderna (MRNA) +156.0%

Top Detractor: DaVita (DVA) -26.7%

Top Theme: Biotech and select life science names led healthcare higher in August, while healthcare services and managed care names were among laggards.

Best performers in August

Moderna (MRNA) was August’s biggest winner, surging 156.0% after positive interim results from a late-stage trial of its personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, mRNA-4157, in combination with Merck’s (MRK) Keytruda. Veeva Systems (VEEV) gained 40.2% after a strong Q2 performance and raised outlook, while Charles River Laboratories (CRL) advanced 24% on improving expectations for biopharma outsourcing demand. Revvity (RVTY) rose 14.4% and Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) gained 14.1%, supported by positive developments across their respective pipelines and businesses.

Seeking Alpha analyst Stephen Ayers said, "I think Moderna's (MRNA) and Merck's (MRK) 'personalized vaccine' breakthrough in melanoma likely grabbed generalists' attention, with many betting that it validates their broader mRNA platform beyond viral vaccines (i.e., COVID-19). Both Veeva (VEEV) and Charles River Laboratories (CRL) delivered beat-and-raises on the strength of robust biopharma demand. Veeva, in particular, was also a beaten down 'SaaS' name that the market was discounting due to AI-related existential concerns and competition from Microsoft (MSFT)."

Top 5 gainers:

  • Moderna (MRNA): +156.0%
  • Veeva Systems (VEEV): +40.2%
  • Charles River Laboratories (CRL): +24.0%
  • Revvity (RVTY): +14.4%
  • Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX): +14.1%

Detractors in August

On the other hand, DaVita (DVA) was the biggest detractor, falling 26.7% amid concerns over its dialysis business and earnings outlook. Insulet (PODD) and CVS Health (CVS) both declined 10.1% on business and earnings concerns, while UnitedHealth (UNH) and Viatris (VTRS) each fell 6% amid continued pressure on their respective businesses.

The weakness was concentrated in healthcare services, managed care, and selected pharmaceutical stocks. The services group was weighed down in particular by dialysis providers, while managed-care names remained under pressure.

"The top detractors—DaVita (DVA), Insulet (PODD), and CVS Health (CVS)—are facing margin compression and/or unfavorable payer mix shifts. What's interesting is that GLP-1s like Eli Lilly's (LLY) Zepbound may be playing a subtle role in all three. While all three are experiencing metric deterioration, GLP-1s (ironically, another major innovation) may be causing investors to consider the long-term consequences. For DaVita and Insulet, growing GLP-1 adoption could reduce dependence on hemodialysis and automated insulin delivery devices (diabetes), respectively, by prolonging, or, in some cases, completely eliminating the need's onset. Meanwhile, the rising utilization of high-cost GLP-1s is a structural margin headwind for CVS Health's PBM business, CVS Caremark," Ayers said.

Top 5 losers:

  • DaVita (DVA): -26.7%
  • Insulet (PODD): -10.1%
  • CVS Health (CVS): -10.1%
  • UnitedHealth Group (UNH): -6.0%
  • Viatris (VTRS): -6.0%

Looking ahead, investors will focus on healthcare earnings, clinical-trial readouts, regulatory decisions and pipeline developments, while watching whether biotechnology’s August rally broadens beyond a handful of stocks.

data.title: Bessent predicts $40 crude oil and lower yields after Iran war
data.description:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expects oil prices to crater to as low as $40 after the U.S.–Iran war and bond yields to decline concurrently from record highs reached this week.

In an interview with former Trump advisor Steve Bannon that aired on Friday, Bessent also addressed concerns over a proposal by Norway’s sovereign wealth fund to cut back on its holdings of Treasuries.

“We’re going to get on the other side of this Iran conflict, and I expect that oil will come down,” he said, adding, “We’re going to be very much oversupplied in the oil market after this. We can see $50, $40 crude maybe, just because there’s so much coming online.”

Oil prices spiked this week as hostilities between the U.S. and Iran resumed after a period of relative calm, sparking concerns over a prolonged disruption to petroleum shipments out of the Persian Gulf.

With renewed Middle East tensions triggering inflationary fears, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) reached a post-pandemic high on Monday, sending shockwaves across global markets.

“If you go and look, the interest rates—this is the highest correlation they’ve ever had to the oil price,” Bessent said, adding, “The Iran conflict will end, interest rates and the spike in headline inflation will come down.”

On Norway’s sovereign wealth fund’s moves to lower its Treasury holdings, Bessent said, “They're just looking to upgrade their yield with other American assets.”

If the fund that manages a $2.3T investment portfolio is planning to buy financial instruments from government-backed home financing enterprises such as Fannie Mae (FNMA) and Freddie Mac (FMCC), “I am the biggest advocate for that,” he said.

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersect with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Akamai, Robinhood and Nio among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) rose 0.7% for the week, while the Dow (DJI) gained marginally. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Robinhood raised to Overweight at Morgan Stanley

Morgan Stanley upgraded Robinhood Markets (HOOD) to Overweight from Equalweight as the financial app platform's broadening range of products drives growth in assets per customer, increased activity per customer, and greater economics captured per activity.

Morgan Stanley increased its price target for Robinhood stock to $150 from $124.

"Rather than relying primarily on funded-account growth or a stronger retail trading environment, HOOD increasingly has multiple ways to grow revenue from its 28M customers already on the platform," analyst Michael J. Cyprys wrote.

Akamai upgraded on Compute business gains

Akamai (AKAM) was upgraded to Overweight from Neutral by Piper Sandler due in part to recent wins from its Compute business segment.

"Akamai has yet to disclose its Compute megawatts that we expect will be given in time," said Piper Sandler analyst James Fish.

"Today, we estimate Akamai has approximately 22 active MWs out of about 47 MWs of capacity, though given $2.8B+ of commitments/35 MWs. Akamai is 'sold-out' already and needs more capacity to get these online. As such, we are raising our capex estimates to $2.3B in '27-'28 each, which assumes a rising capex/MW cost and about 30 active MWs/year incrementally."

Piper Sandler lowered its price target on the stock to $125 from $140.

Nio downgraded on ‘slower’ 2H growth

Nio (NIO) was downgraded to Hold from Buy by Freedom Broker, which cut its price target to $4 from $7, citing weaker-than-expected third-quarter guidance that could signal “slower growth in 2H26.”

Analyst Dmitriy Pozdnyakov expects third-quarter revenue of 31.5 billion yuan and deliveries of 108,000 vehicles. They cut its 2026 revenue forecast to 123 billion yuan from 138 billion yuan and delivery forecast to 419,000 vehicles from 468,000.

Pozdnyakov said NIO (NIO) continues to show “strong EV shipment growth” and is “actively expanding” its ONVO and FIREFLY brands. They expect rising volumes to support positive net income through “improved absorption of operating expenses.”

Ambarella (AMBA) was downgraded by investment firm Craig Hallum to Hold from Buy after the semiconductor design company's second-quarter results and guidance indicated a lack of clarity on a couple of key items. The brokerage cut price target to $70 from $95.

HSBC Global Investment Research downgraded Trip.com (TCOM) to Hold from Buy, citing regulatory pressures and expectations for a softer-than-expected travel season that could weigh on upcoming results.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Nvidia, Dell, Broadcom in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week as investors digested earnings reports from heavyweights including Dell (DELL) and Broadcom (AVGO).

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the red on Friday. For the week, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) rose marginally during the week. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Sandisk (SNDK) +17.17%
  • Dell (DELL) +14.84%
  • Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) +12.51%
  • Micron Technology (MU) +8.85%
  • Intel (INTC) +7.07%

Top Losers:

  • Fair Isaac (FICO) -19.22%
  • Autodesk (ADSK) -16.40%
  • Ciena (CIEN) -15.16%
  • Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) -14.01%
  • Synopsys (SNPS) -11.02%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B

Nvidia (NVDA) confirmed prior media reports on Thursday when it announced it had agreed to purchase Hugging Face for $12.9B.

Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Dell soars 16% on record results; HPE raises guidance

Dell (DELL) shares were nearly 16% higher on Wednesday after the IT giant delivered a stronger-than-expected second quarter and sharply raised its fiscal 2027 outlook, underscoring the strength of demand for AI infrastructure.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan raised his price target to $600 from $505 and reiterated his Buy rating, stating that Dell is benefiting from the supply constraints facing the AI industry.

HPE's (HPE) third quarter 2026 results also featured momentum across all its business segments and an increase in its outlook.

Broadcom guidance for 2027, 2028 surprises Wall Street

Broadcom (AVGO) offered weaker-than-expected guidance that overshadowed its third-quarter results. Looking ahead, Broadcom said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to be approximately $34.8B, with adjusted EBITDA around 66%. Analysts had expected $35.1B in fourth-quarter sales, according to Bloomberg.

However, the company’s offering of guidance for 2028 surprised Wall Street. Following the results and guidance, several Wall Street firms raised their price targets on Broadcom, including Cantor Fitzgerald, which went to $600 from $525. Macquarie upgraded shares to Outperform and put a $490 price target on the stock.

Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said that the guidance for 2027 shows Broadcom is on track, but the 2028 guidance was a positive surprise, even if there is some skepticism attached to it.

Other notable tech headlines include "Big Short" investor Michael Burry renewing his bearish view on Palantir (PLTR) and criticizing the company’s valuation, business model, accounting, stock-based compensation, and CEO Alex Karp’s aircraft-related expenses, among other things.

HP (HPQ) also posted Q3 results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates.

However, the company said looking ahead to the remainder of our fiscal year, it continues to expect input costs to rise, putting near-term pressure on its operating margins, particularly in Personal Systems. 

Apple (AAPL) is reportedly facing a £2B (~$2.7B) lawsuit in the UK over its app tracking practices, with lawyers for app developers alleging that the company used its position as a gatekeeper to give its own advertising business an advantage.

data.title: Banks, crypto in gainers; Aon, credit card stocks among losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the trading week mixed, as tech giant Broadcom posted its latest earnings in a week when yields and rates remained in focus after the latest nonfarm payrolls report landed.

"The real economy took a hit this week, an artifact of the better-than-expected jobs report released on Friday. The sell-off that followed was largely caused by the hawks, who see the good news as reasons for a rate hike," said Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman.

"The prospect of higher rates while inflation is primarily being driven by energy inflation means a squeeze on consumers and anything that lives off financing costs," said Bowman.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) closed the week flat at $58.10. However, bank stocks were gaining. The Invesco KBW Bank ETF (KBWB) added 1.42% week-over-week to $97.65.

Investors may consider banks with higher fee income components more attractive than traditional spread lenders, or institutions that derive at least two-thirds of their revenue from net interest income, according to Brean Capital analyst Christopher Marinac.

"There could be a perception or narrative that so-called 'fee banks' are better stocks for an uncertain period of Federal Reserve interest rate policy and debate over sustained [earnings-per-share] growth in the industry," Marinac wrote in a research report.

Among megacap stocks, the foreign stock Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) led the gainers, potentially benefiting from a weaker dollar.

The stock added 5.20% from the prior week to close at $24.09.

With the U.S. Treasury Department's ongoing expanded bond buybacks, "it is reasonable to assume we could see some dollar weakness, and that could continue to kind of help support returns in international equities from a dollar-[based] investor standpoint," Josh Jones, portfolio manager at Boston Partners, told CNBC News.

The US Dollar Index (DXY) inched down ~0.5% during the week.

Payment stocks, Mastercard (MA) (-2.70% W/W to $579.21), American Express (AXP) (-2.11% W/W to $326.16), and Visa (V) (-1.71% W/W to $375.07), led the decliners as the stablecoin disruption saw a major development this week. A group of 21 international financial institutions announced plans to establish a new stablecoin company in the second half of 2026. 

The newly-created stablecoin is expected to launch in the first half of 2027.

The venture comes as a competition to Open Standard's Open USD (OPEN-USD) stablecoin that has signed over 140 companies to participate, including Visa (V), Mastercard (MA), and American Express (AXP).

Aon (AON) topped the largecap losers, retreating 9.09% week-over-week to $323.09.

The stock dropped 10% on Monday after the professional services and insurance brokerage firm announced a $17B acquisition of USI Insurance Services from KKR (KKR).

Crypto stocks, IREN (IREN) (+26.04% W/W to $44.68), Hut 8 (HUT) (+17.79% W/W to $93.55), Robinhood Markets (HOOD) (+17.12% W/W to $122.11), Circle Internet (CRCL) (+17.11% W/W to $102.05), and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) (+13.44% W/W to $26.33), were the biggest advancers as bitcoin (BTC-USD) added ~3% during the course of the week.

For Seeking Alpha analysts' thoughts on whether the cryptocurrency was finally making a comeback, click here.

Midcap stocks, Strive (ASST) (+24.84% W/W to $27.14) and Riot Platforms (RIOT) (+14.80% W/W to $21.80), stood out as winners in the category.

Goosehead Insurance (GSHD) was the top midcap loser, pulling back 8.49% to close at $65.21. The insurer reported insider transactions this week.

Among smallcap stocks, AlTi Global (ALTI) (-25.19% W/W to $3.00). TOP Financial (TOP) (-10.40% W/W to $14.99), Chaince Digital (CD) (+24.85% W/W to $4.07), and Bit Digital (BTBT) (+14.69% W/W to $1.64) were the notable movers.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 7 of 8 key S&P 500 reporting firms top EPS estimates as all 8 post Y/Y profit growth
data.description:
Corporate earnings featured a notable lineup of reports from 8 key S&P 500 reporting firms across the information technology, health care, consumer discretionary, and consumer staples sectors.

Earnings Roundup:

  • Bottom Line: Earnings performance was exceptionally strong, as 7 out of 8 reporting companies beat consensus EPS estimates while 1 matched expectations in-line. All 8 companies achieved year-over-year profit expansion.

  • Top Line: Revenue performance was more mixed, with 5 companies exceeding Wall Street expectations and 3 falling short of consensus estimates. Overall, 7 of the 8 firms delivered year-over-year top-line growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Dell Technologies (DELL) jumped 15.81% after their fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings exceeded expectations. They reported a 58% increase in revenue to $46.97 billion and an adjusted EPS of $7.04. The Infrastructure Solutions Group experienced an 89% increase, and the company projects third-quarter revenue of $49 billion and full-year sales of $192 billion, boosted by AI server demand.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) slipped 9.28% despite topping fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 expectations and issuing an optimistic forward forecast. Revenue jumped 34% year-over-year to $3.41 billion, driven by $2.67 billion in subscription and support revenue and $738 million in product sales, while adjusted EPS came in at $1.02, beating consensus estimates. For the first quarter, the cybersecurity leader projects revenue between $3.30 billion and $3.31 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.96 to $0.98, alongside strong growth targets for full-year fiscal 2027.

Medtronic (MDT) rose 1.53% post-earnings after reporting strong first-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street expectations. Revenue increased by 13.8% year-over-year to $9.76 billion, surpassing estimates by $220 million. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.45, beating consensus by $0.06. Cardiovascular revenue grew by 18.9%. Medtronic raised its full-year growth guidance to 7.25%-7.75% and adjusted its FY27 non-GAAP EPS outlook to $5.94–$6.00 (from $5.90–$6.00 previously) against a $5.95 consensus.

Broadcom (AVGO) dropped 2.7% post-earnings due to lower-than-expected revenue guidance for Q4, despite strong Q3 results. In Q3, adjusted EPS was $3.32, with revenue up 86% at $29.59 billion, boosted by strong semiconductor and infrastructure sales. Q4 revenue is expected around $34.8 billion, below analyst expectations.

Lululemon Athletica (LULU) shares dropped nearly 20% in post-market trading after the company lowered its full-year sales forecast due to declining sales in China and increased competition. Lululemon expects a 5% to 7% sales decline, estimating $10.35B to $10.50B, down from $11.0B to $11.50B. Current-quarter sales are projected to fall 10% to 11%. In the second quarter, revenue declined 4%, with comparable sales down 9%, despite an EPS of $2.92 exceeding estimates.

Brown-Forman (BF.A) (BF.B) rose 3.87% post-earnings after reporting mixed first-quarter results, with earnings per share rising 6% to $0.38, beating estimates. Gross margin increased due to lower costs. Sales were affected by weak tequila and barrel sales, the end of a distribution agreement, and declines in some markets, despite growth in ready-to-drink products. Management expects flat sales and a 3% to 5% decline in operating income for the full year.

NetApp (NTAP) gained 2.55% post-earnings after delivering a strong first-quarter results for fiscal 2027, with a 30% increase in revenue to $2.03 billion and adjusted EPS at $2.58, exceeding estimates. However, shares dropped 8% post-report due to a 35% decrease in free cash flow. The company provided strong guidance for Q2 and raised its full-year revenue and EPS forecasts.

Campbell's Company (CPB) saw a sharp decline in stock value, down 6.96%, after missing fourth-quarter revenue estimates, with net sales down 8% to $2.1 billion. Profit margins decreased significantly due to cost inflation, leading to a 25% drop in adjusted EBIT and a 37% decline in adjusted EPS. The board approved a 36% cut in the quarterly dividend and announced a cost-savings initiative targeting $500 million by FY30, while fiscal guidance also fell below expectations.
